pi.name: Mohammed Akaaboune
pi.title: Professor of Molecular, Cellular, and Developmental Biology
pi.bio: Mohammed Akaaboune earned his DEA and Ph.D. from the University of Pierre and Marie Curie (Paris 6) in France, and completed postdoctoral training in Jeff Lichtman's laboratory at Washington University School of Medicine in St. Louis, supported by a Human Frontier Science Program fellowship. He is a Professor in the Department of Molecular, Cellular, and Developmental Biology at the University of Michigan. His lab studies the regulation and dynamics of synaptic proteins at healthy and compromised neuromuscular junctions using optical imaging, molecular, cellular, and biochemical approaches in mice.

lab_description: The Akaaboune Lab investigates the cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying the dynamics and trafficking of postsynaptic proteins at healthy and compromised synapses. The lab uses the neuromuscular junction as its primary model because it is the simplest and best-characterized synapse in vertebrates. The team combines advanced in vivo imaging that follows the same synapses over extended periods with molecular and biochemical approaches in living mice. Current work addresses how high-fat diet, aging, and loss of dystrophin glycoprotein complex components alter the stability of nicotinic acetylcholine receptors and scaffold proteins such as rapsyn and alpha-kap at the postsynaptic membrane.

research_areas.title: High-fat diet and neuromuscular junction stability
research_areas.summary: Examines how obesity induced by a high-fat diet affects the structural integrity and disassembly of the neuromuscular junction in mouse models.

research_areas.title: Dystrophin glycoprotein complex function
research_areas.summary: Studies the role of the dystrophin glycoprotein complex (including alpha-dystrobrevin and alpha-syntrophin) in maintaining nicotinic acetylcholine receptor stability at synapses.

research_areas.title: Aging and the postsynaptic apparatus
research_areas.summary: Investigates how aging alters the stability and organization of postsynaptic components at the neuromuscular junction.

research_areas.title: Molecular interactions in living systems
research_areas.summary: Analyzes spatial and temporal interactions between postsynaptic molecular components using live imaging in mice.

research_areas.title: Rapsyn function in non-muscle contexts
research_areas.summary: Explores the role of the scaffold protein rapsyn in cellular environments outside muscle, including lysosome clustering.
